In #39370 and #39371 I add some small specialized grind sets. Currently I have only created compactness and closedness, to prove IsCompact goals and IsClosed goals. I think this would be useful to add to Mathlib, and to also add for a whole lot more predicates.

Uses:

  • Can be added as a cheap auto-param for hypotheses of lemmas: (h : IsCompact K := by compactness)
  • Can be used as a cheap discharger for tactics like fun_prop
  • Can be combined with other grind attributes: grind only [compactness, closedness]

I think this has advantages over using a single global grind set, since we can tag lemmas more aggressively in these small grind sets. This would likely not be performant when doing this for the global grind set(?)

More information in the module doc of the new file.

Do you think this is useful? I'm particular interested in @Kim Morrison's opinion.

Developed at ICERM, in discussion with @David Ledvinka, @Moritz Doll, @Tomas Skrivan, @Winston Yin (尹維晨) and @Bhavik Mehta.

As mentioned in person, I think grind sets are a great idea. I left a couple of small comments on the first PR. I also think it is important that these are compatible with #grind_lint. Kim had asked me to open an issue for this, which I have now done: lean4#13733
We could have a grind set for substructure membership (add_mem, mul_mem etc) to replace the existing Aesop SetLike ruleset.
